leads.name: Treebeard-like oak, Sher Brook Valley, Cannock Chase
leads.reason: Staffordshire Live article (huge-tree-looks-just-like-6630743) seen only as a search snippet, page redirects to tollbit and was not read; no coordinate, age or measurements. Near the stepping stones among Brocton Coppice oaks.

leads.name: Brocton Coppice ancient oaks (other trunks)
leads.reason: Coppice holds about 600 sessile oaks per Staffordshire County Council statements (search summaries); no other individually named or located trunk found. Komoot highlight 4067914 'Ancient Oak Woodland' at 52.77215,-2.028891 is a woodland-level point, not a tree.

leads.name: Tettenhall yews photograph
leads.reason: Needs an open-licence photo of the three yews on the north side of St Michael's; unchecked Geograph views exist (Commons 7864664, 408902, 6831878).

leads.name: Bushbury St Mary yew remains
leads.reason: Ancient Yew Group Staffordshire PDF notes a 1905 visit recorded yew remains; whether still alive is unknown; not checked further.

leads.name: Merridale Cemetery hornbeam (Jeffcock Road entrance)
leads.reason: The Street Tree substack post 91 (10 Feb 2024, Paul Wood) calls it one of Wolverhampton's finest trees and 'very old'; post paywalled, no size, age or coordinate. Cemetery opened 1850. Lead only.

leads.name: Boningale St Chad yew (Shropshire)
leads.reason: AYG: 396 cm at ground, shown in a 1791 painting; about 10 miles west of Wolverhampton in Shropshire, no practical public transport verified; modest girth.

leads.name: Pendeford yew
leads.reason: AYG: 508 cm at 122 cm, 2019, but notes say public with restricted access on a footpath/road site; no safe access statement.

leads.name: Royal Oak descendant ('Son of Royal Oak'), Boscobel House
leads.reason: In Shropshire, English Heritage site, thought to be 2 or 3 centuries old; no public transport within 30 minutes of Wolverhampton verified; Moseley Old Hall has only a tree house inspired by the story. Candidate for a Shropshire pass.

leads.name: Shugborough: other veteran trees and visitor-centre ancient oak
leads.reason: A contractor news item says the new visitor centre wraps around an ancient oak; no species, girth or location confirmed.

leads.name: Sandwell Valley Country Park sweet chestnuts
leads.reason: A Woodland Trust visiting page (not the Ancient Tree Inventory) said some trees in Park Farm Wood and Priory Wood are over 200 years old, 'amazing sweet chestnuts'; no individual tree, no location. Not fetched.

leads.name: Codsall Coppice LNR oak woodland (Sandwell)
leads.reason: Woodland of over 2 ha mainly oak, thought over 400 years old as woodland; a wood, not a collectible tree.

blocked.name: West Park Wolverhampton common oak and sessile oak
blocked.reason: Planted 1897 for Victoria's Diamond Jubilee per the council tree trail page, not ancient; leads only if a reader wants them.

blocked.name: Wightwick Manor, Bantock Park, Oak House, Dartmouth Park trees
blocked.reason: No individual veteran tree named in any source found; paid or park-level only.
